content:
In Class 6, algebra was letters and patterns. In Class 7 it becomes machinery: collecting like terms, multiplying brackets, spotting coefficients. The IMO tests whether the machinery runs without slips. Scroll down for the free IMO Class 7 Algebraic Expressions online test. Ten Olympiad-pattern MCQs, instant scoring. Under every question sits an explanation you can learn from.

What the IMO asks from Algebraic Expressions in Class 7

  • Terms, factors, coefficients and degree.
  • Adding and subtracting expressions (like terms).
  • Value of an expression by substitution.
  • Simplifying with brackets and minus signs.
  • Framing expressions from word statements.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Only like terms combine: 7x² and 3x live in different worlds.
  • The coefficient of the highest-degree term of 7y² − 3y + 15 is 7.
  • A minus before a bracket flips EVERY sign inside.
  • Constant term = the term with no variable (in 7x + 14 it is 14).

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Combining x² with x because "both have x".
  • Flipping only the first sign when removing a minus bracket.
  • Substituting into x² as 2x instead of x times x.

quiz.title: IMO Class 7 Algebraic Expressions Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 7: Algebraic Expressions

questions.q: In the expression 7y<sup>2</sup> − 3y + 15, what is the coefficient of the term with the highest degree?
questions.explanation: The highest-degree term is 7y<sup>2</sup> (degree 2). Its coefficient is 7.
It has two unlike terms, 2x and 3y. An expression with two terms is a binomial.

questions.q: If A = 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 7 and B = −x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 4, find A + B.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> terms: 3 − 1 = 2. x terms: 2 + 5 = 7. Constants: −7 + 4 = −3. A + B = 2x<sup>2</sup> + 7x − 3.

questions.q: If x = −2 and y = 3, evaluate 3x<sup>2</sup> − 2xy + y<sup>2</sup>.
What is the product of the monomials 4a<sup>2</sup> b and −3ab<sup>3</sup>?
questions.explanation: Coefficients: 4 × (−3) = −12. Variables: a<sup>2</sup> × a = a<sup>3</sup> and b × b<sup>3</sup> = b<sup>4</sup>. Product: −12a<sup>3</sup> b<sup>4</sup>.
The middle term of (a + b)<sup>2</sup> is 2ab. 2 × 2x × 3y = 12xy, so A = 12.

questions.q: In the identity (x + a)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 16, find the value of a.
questions.explanation: Compare middle terms: 2a = 8, so a = 4. Check: a<sup>2</sup> = 16 ✓.

questions.q: Sachin has x books. He buys 12 more, then loses 5. Which expression gives his total now?
questions.explanation: After buying: x + 12. After losing 5: x + 12 − 5 = x + 7.

questions.q: If a + b = 5 and a − b = 3, find a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: (a + b)<sup>2</sup> + (a − b)<sup>2</sup> = 2(a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>). 25 + 9 = 34, so a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> = 17.
